reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

Keep every grid, demo, and derived output in this instance's conversational state; other instances may reuse the task ID but have distinct inputs, demos, and attempt state.
2. For a new task or unusable cache, infer one coherent rule from all demos and implement it. After each demo, run the candidate on every retained pair and compare shape and every cell. Treat exact reproduction of all retained pairs as a hard gate: do not submit a test prediction from an unvalidated candidate, even if its transform runs successfully. Request another demo only if it can distinguish live hypotheses; requests and wrong submissions cost score. First identify the structural layout from the examples: horizontal/vertical separators, panel boundaries, and relative panel sizes. Derive color and overlap operations by testing exact demo cells, including background and non-background examples; do not assume a divider or a fixed color mapping generalizes across examples. Treat color 0 as an ordinary color unless the demos establish that it is transparent or background; a template may use zero-valued cells as visible foreground.
3. Before submitting, run the current transform on the test and submit exactly its output. Serialize or copy the program's result directly into the action; do not hand-reconstruct the grid, since a single mistyped row width makes it invalid. After an incorrect verdict, inspect the exact submitted output and source, treat the verdict as counterevidence, and reconsider the whole rule against every demo and test; do not patch guesses or submit unverified output. If the failed candidate came from a cached program and no demos are available, request a demo before editing or trying another prediction; a repeated run or unchanged rewrite of that candidate adds no evidence. After repeated failures, pause before another attempt: state the competing hypotheses, identify evidence in demos that distinguishes them, and test the full candidate against all retained pairs. Treat feedback saying an output is not a valid grid as an output-format/serialization failure first: verify outer type, dimensions, row lengths, and integer range against the stated constraints; do not infer a puzzle-rule failure until those checks pass. If demos leave competing rules, make each candidate predict the complete outputs for every retained pair and compare the cells that differ between hypotheses; spend another demo only when its possible result would choose between them. After the demo cap, prefer the simplest rule that actually reproduces all demonstrations, and label any test extrapolation uncertain rather than claiming verification.
4. Once the instance is over (correct verdict or attempt cap), re-run the exact final candidate against every received demo before saving. Save/replace the task file only if that candidate reproduces every demo exactly; otherwise leave the prior file unchanged. A correct test verdict does not establish demo consistency.     rs = [r for r in range(h) if all(grid[r][c] == grid[r][0] for c in range(w)) and grid[r][0] != bg]

    rs = [r for r in range(h) if grid[r][0] != bg]
    cs = [c for c in range(w) if grid[0][c] != bg]
